ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.claim: God controls joy and grief, life and death, provision and children, prosperity and poverty, so everyone should turn to Him at all times.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.anchor: sorrow and happiness, life and death, subsistence and children, affluence and poverty are all under the control of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r2.claim: Only God grants life and death, which rules out anyone else’s lordship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r2.anchor: it is only in God’s authority to grant life and death.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.claim: With slight variations, these divine acts echo Abraham’s declaration of acquittal against his people in 26:78–82.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.anchor: Who has created me; then he guides me

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r1.claim: God alone causes death and life; the emphatic pronoun and repeated attribution establish exclusive agency.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r1.anchor: وتقديم الضمير وتكرير الإسناد للحصر أي أنه تعالى فعل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r5.claim: No one besides God causes death or life: a killer only dismantles the human body, while God brings about death through His customary order.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68#3/r5.anchor: فلا يقدر على الإماتة والإحياء غير عز وجل والقاتل إنماينقض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r1.claim: God causes death in this world and brings people to life for resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r1.anchor: أي: أمات في الدنيا وأحيا للبعث.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God caused the fathers to die and brought the children to life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r3.claim: Another explanation contrasts the indefinite “died” for the unbeliever with the definite “lived” for the believer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: أمات الكافر بالنكرة وأحيا المؤمن بالمعرفة.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r1.claim: He caused death and life are used intransitively, as in 53:43, displaying God's wondrous power and hinting at the possibility of resurrection, which human creation witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r1.anchor: وفعلا { أمات وأحيا } منزلان منزلة اللازم كما تقدم في قوله : { وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى } ( النجم : 43 ) إظهارا لبديع القدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r2.claim: The separating pronoun asserts that God alone gives life and death, against pagans who attributed them to time; the past-tense statement is not about afterlife, which they denied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r2.anchor: وضمير الفصل للقصر على نحو قوله : { وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى } ( النجم : 43 ) ردا على أهل الجاهلية الذين يسندون الإحياء والإماتة إلى الدهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r3.claim: The verse also uses antithesis, setting life against death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r3.anchor: وفي هذه الآية محسن الطباق أيضا لما بين الحياة والموت من التضاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83/r1.claim: God causes death in this worldly life and gives life for the resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وأنه هو أمات في الدنيا وأحيا للبعث

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r6.claim: Only God creates death and life; a killer merely breaks bodily structure and connection, while death occurs through God's customary act, and the servant's part is only the acquired act of dismantling the body.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r6.anchor: لا يقدر على الإحياء والإماتة غيره لا خلقا ولا كسبا

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r7.claim: Other explanations say God kills at the appointed time and revives in the grave, creates the causes of death and life, kills unbelievers through denial and revives believers through recognition, or brings about ignorance and knowledge, miserliness and generosity, withholding and giving.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r7.anchor: يا او سازنده اسباب موت وحياتست وكفته اند مرده ميسازد كافر انرا

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r8.claim: Further reported pairs are fertility and famine, fathers and sons, waking and sleeping, or sperm and the living being.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r8.anchor: وقيل الخصب والجدب أو الآباء والأبناء أو أيقظ وأنام

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r9.speaker: المحققون
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r9.claim: The realized Sufis interpret death and life as awe and intimacy, or concealment and manifestation.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r9.anchor: ونزد محققان بهيبت وأنس ياباستتار وتجلي

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r10.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r10.claim: Al-Qushayrī says God kills ascetics' egos through discipline and revives gnostics' hearts through witnessing, or brings a person to annihilation and gives subsistence through God.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r10.anchor: وأمام قشيري فرموده كه بميراند نفوس زاهد انرا بآثار مجاهدت

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r11.claim: The inward reading is death of the self from bodily desires and animal pleasures and life of the heart through spiritual qualities and divine character; while the heart fluctuates, self and heart may dominate each other, but in settled assurance the self remains subdued by the heart.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r11.anchor: أو أمات النفس عن الشهوات الجسمانية واللذات الحيوانية

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r12.claim: Death precedes life for rhyme, because sperm precedes the living being, the heart dies before living, and bodily death precedes resurrection in the grave; placing death first also hastens the warning's impact.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r12.anchor: قدم الإماتة على الإحياء رعاية للفاصلة ولأن النطفة قبل النسمة

BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r13.claim: Nonexistence precedes existence and existence ends in annihilation; people should not be deceived by a life between two deaths or existence between two absences.
BURSEVI:v9p208#2/r13.anchor: وأيضا أن العدم قبل الوجود ثم أن مآل الوجود إلى الفناء والعدم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r1.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God causes fathers to die and brings sons to life.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that He causes death through disbelief and gives life through faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#7/r3.claim: A third interpretation is that He causes death in this world and gives life in the next.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r4.claim: God caused the circumstances that bring about death and life.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r5.speaker: ابن بحر
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r5.claim: Ibn Bahr reads the phrase as God creating death and life, as in 67:2.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r5.anchor: الذي خلق الموت والحياة [الملك:2] قاله ابن بحر.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that God makes the unbeliever dead through unbelief and gives the believer life through faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r6.anchor: أمات الكافر بالكفر وأحيا المؤمن بالإيمان قال الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r7.claim: Ata explains death as God acting with justice and life as His bestowal of favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r7.anchor: قول عطاء: أمات بعدله وأحيا بفضله.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r8.claim: One view takes death and life as withholding and miserliness versus generosity and giving.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r8.anchor: وقول من قال: أمات بالمنع والبخل وأحيا بالجود والبذل.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r9.claim: Another view says God causes the sperm to die and brings the living offspring to life.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r10.claim: Another interpretation is that God causes fathers to die and sons to live.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r11.claim: The phrase may describe drought and fertility, respectively.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r11.anchor: وقيل: يريد بالحياة الخصب وبالموت الجدب.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r12.claim: Another interpretation is sleep followed by waking.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r13.claim: Another reading is death in this world and revival for resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:44-45/r13.anchor: وقيل: أمات في الدنيا وأحيا للبعث.

QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r10.claim: God causes death in this world and life in the grave, where a person either rests or experiences punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r10.anchor: أماته في الدنيا ، وأحياه في القبر ؛ فالقبر إما للراحة وإما للإحساس بالعقوبة

QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r11.claim: Another explanation is death in this life followed by life at the resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r11.anchor: ويقال : أماته في الدنيا ، وأحياه في الحشر

QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r12.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r12.claim: A Sufi reading says ascetics' selves die through spiritual struggle, while gnostics' hearts live through witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r12.anchor: ويقال : أمات نفوس الزاهدين بالمجاهدة ، وأحيا قلوب العارفين بالمشاهدة

QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r13.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r13.claim: Other inward pairings are death through awe and life through intimacy, concealment and manifestation, turning away and turning toward, and obedience and sin.
QUSHAYRI:v3p253/r13.anchor: ويقال : أماتها بالهيبة ، وأحياها بالأنس . ويقال : بالاستتار ، والتجلي . ويقال : بالإعراض عنه ، والإقبال عليه . ويقال : بالطاعة ، والمعصية

SULAMI:v2p289#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r1.claim: Al-Qasim says God makes people die to remembrance and obedience, revives them through remembrance and obedience, and then leaves them without excuse.
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : يميته عن ذكره وطاعته ويحييه بذكره وطاعته ثم لا يعذرهم .

SULAMI:v2p289#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says God causes death through His justice and gives life through His grace.
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أمات بعدله وأحيا بفضله .

SULAMI:v2p289#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r3.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r3.claim: Al-Nasrabadi interprets death as veiling and life as self-disclosure.
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r3.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : يميت بالاستتار ويحيي بالتجلي .

SULAMI:v2p289#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r4.claim: Ja'far says God gives death through turning away and life through gnosis, killing souls through disobedience and reviving hearts with the lights of conformity.
SULAMI:v2p289#2/r4.anchor: قال جعفر : أمات بالإعراض عنه وأحيا بالمعرفة به وقال : امات النفوس بالمخالفة وأحيا القلوب بأنوار الموافقة .

TUSTARI:53:44/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:44/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:44/r1.claim: God deadens the hearts of His enemies through disbelief and darkness, and gives His friends life through faith and the lights of gnosis.
TUSTARI:53:44/r1.anchor: أمات قلوب الأعداء بالكفر والظلمة، وأحيا قلوب الأولياء بالإيمان وأنوار المعرفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r1.speaker: المتقدمون من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r1.claim: Earlier commentators interpret the phrase as death in worldly life followed by resurrection to life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r2.speaker: المتأخرون من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r2.claim: Later commentators also say God caused fathers to die and brought sons to life, like the wording in 45:24.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r2.anchor: والمتأخرون منهم ذكروا وجوها أخرى، منها: أنه أمات الآباء، وأحيا الأبناء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r3.speaker: المتأخرون من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r3.claim: Other later interpretations say God caused the sperm to die and brought the living being to life, or made an unbeliever dead through disbelief and a believer alive through faith, paralleling 30:19 and 6:122.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p72/r3.anchor: ومنها أنه أمات النطفة وأحيا النسمة، وأمات الكافر بالكفر وأحيا المؤمن بالإيمان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r1.claim: When an omitted noun or verb is correctly recoverable, its omission is often better and more natural than saying it explicitly; the suppressed element should be restored only where the context calls for it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r1.anchor: وأنت تجد حذفه هناك أحسن من ذكره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r2.speaker: سمية
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r2.claim: In the fragment attributed to Sumayya, the author supplies the omitted sense as ‘that is delusion I keep returning to, so leave off blaming me.’
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r2.anchor: قالت سمية : قد غويت ، بأن رأت حقا تناوب مالنا ووفودا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r3.claim: With أضحك وأبكى, أمات وأحيا, and أغنى وأقنى, the objects are omitted so the verbs assert God as the source of laughter and tears, life and death, and enrichment and contentment generally, without specifying an object.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p126/r3.anchor: هو الذي منه الإحياء والإماتة والإغناء والإقناء

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.claim: Except verse 46, each verse in 42–50 begins wa anna, continuing the discussion of Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures in 36–41.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.anchor: Each verse in this passage, except v. 46, begins with wa anna

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.claim: Wa anna may instead be read wa inna, making each instance an independent thought meaning truly, surely, or verily.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.anchor: But wa anna could also be read wa inna, which would make each occurrence mark a new, independent thought

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r11.claim: God’s causing death and life demonstrates His power over every phase of existence and nonexistence.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r11.anchor: That it is He Who causes death and gives life

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r12.speaker: ST
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r12.claim: Another reading says God causes His enemies’ hearts to die through disbelief and gives His friends’ hearts life through faith and gnosis.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r12.anchor: He causes the hearts of His enemies to die

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.claim: Exclusive divine causation does not rule out natural or non-natural intermediaries such as human joy, organs of laughter, angels, or other causes; these are subject to God and not independent.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.anchor: ولا ينافي ما في هذه الموارد من الحصر توسط أسباب أخر طبيعية أو غير طبيعية فيها

TABATABAI:53:43-49/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r7.claim: As with laughter and weeping, death and life may have natural or non-natural intermediaries, including angels, while their creation remains exclusively God’s.
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r7.anchor: الكلام في انتساب الموت والحياة إلى أسباب أخر طبيعية وغير طبيعية كالملائكة كالكلام في انتساب الضحك والبكاء

TABRISI:53:44-51/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:44-51/r2.claim: God alone creates death and life: whoever could cause death could cause its opposite, but no one can give life except God; He raises the dead for recompense.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r2.anchor: لا يقدر على ذلك غيره لأنه لو قدر على الموت لقدر على الحياة

THALABI:v9p155/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r12.claim: God causes death in this world and gives life for resurrection.
THALABI:v9p155/r12.anchor: وأنه هو أمات أفنى في الدنيا وأحيا للبعث

THALABI:v9p155/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r13.claim: One interpretation is that God caused the fathers to die and brought the children to life.

THALABI:v9p155/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r14.claim: Another interpretation is that God caused the sperm to die and brought the living person to life.

THALABI:v9p155/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r15.claim: An inward interpretation says God deadens the unbeliever through estrangement and separation, and gives the believer life through knowledge and communion.
THALABI:v9p155/r15.anchor: وقيل: أمات الكافر بالنكرة والقطيعة، وأحيا المؤمن بالمعرفة والوصلة

THALABI:v9p155/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r16.claim: The commentary links giving life to the description of someone who was dead and then revived by God.
THALABI:v9p155/r16.anchor: قال سبحانه: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه

THALABI:v9p155/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r17.speaker: القاسم
THALABI:v9p155/r17.claim: Al-Qāsim says God causes death by turning a person from His remembrance and revives him through remembrance.
THALABI:v9p155/r17.anchor: وقال القاسم: أمات عن ذكره وأحيا بذكره

THALABI:v9p155/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r18.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v9p155/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says God causes death through justice and gives life through grace.
THALABI:v9p155/r18.anchor: ابن عطاء: أمات بعدله وأحيا بفضله

THALABI:v9p155/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p155/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p155/r19.claim: Another interpretation says God causes death through withholding and miserliness, and gives life through generosity and giving.
THALABI:v9p155/r19.anchor: وقيل: أمات بالمنع والبخل وأحيا بالجود والبذل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r9.claim: God causes death in this world and gives life for the Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r9.anchor: وأنه هو أمات } في الدنيا { وأحيا } للبعث

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r18.claim: God alone causes death and gives life.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r18.anchor: Ve hakikat öldüren ve dirilten de O’dur başkası değil.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.claim: Verses 43–49 give examples showing that all events across life and death, and all that happens in the universe, depend on God’s will and power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.anchor: insanın hayat-ölüm çizgisi içinde cereyan eden her oluşun ve evrende olup biten her şeyin Allah Teâlâ’nın irade ve kudretine bağlı bulunduğunu gösteren örnekler verilmekte

BURHAN:v3p242/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.claim: Several explanations account for mentioning death before life: the order subdues creatures, human life is like death and leads back to death, and life follows death.
BURHAN:v3p242/r6.anchor: منها أن فيه قهرا للخلق والمقام

BURHAN:v2p449/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.claim: The pronoun هو between إن and its predicate marks these acts as God's alone, since others may claim to give life or cause death; it is omitted for creating the sexes, which no one can claim.
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.anchor: فورد في هذه الجمل الاربع الفصل بالضمير المرفوع بين اسم إن وخبرها

NAHHAS:v4p276/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r20.claim: God causes death and gives life by placing the spirit in a person after that person was a drop of fluid.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r20.anchor: أي أمات من مات وأحيا من حيي بأن جعل فيه الروح بعد أن كان نطفة

NASHR:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p301/r2.claim: The text lists fourteen places of Ruways's optional assimilation: three in al-Baqara, then examples in al-Araf, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, al-Naml, al-Zumar, al-Rum, al-Shura, al-Najm, and al-Infitar.
NASHR:v1p301/r2.anchor: واختلف عنه أيضا في أربعة عشر حرفا وهي ثلاثة في البقرة فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم

NASHR:v1p302/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r2.speaker: أبو العلاء عن النخاس
NASHR:v1p302/r2.claim: Abu al-Ala in his Ghayah, transmitting from al-Nakhkhas, reports assimilation at the first two Najm instances of innahu huwa.
NASHR:v1p302/r2.anchor: إدغام الموضعين إنه هو الأولين من النجم أبو العلاء في غايته عن النخاس

NASHR:v1p302/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r4.speaker: الباقون عن رويس
NASHR:v1p302/r4.claim: Other transmitters from Ruways show all these passages; both assimilation and clear pronunciation are sound transmissions from him.
NASHR:v1p302/r4.anchor: وروى الباقون عن رويس إظهار جميع ذلك، والوجهان عنه صحيحان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.claim: The emphatic هو distinguishes God as the true agent of laughter, weeping, death, life, enrichment, and provision, despite human claims to such power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.anchor: ففي الثلاثة الأول، لما كان قد يدعي ذلك بعض الناس، كقول نمروذ: أنا أحيي وأميت

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r4.claim: God alone causes death and life despite apparent causes; the reversed order is rhetorically apt because death connects with crying and life with laughter.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r4.anchor: وإن رأيتم أسبابا ظاهرية فإنه لا عبرة بها أصلا في نفس الأمر بل هو الذي خلقها . ولما كان ذكر الإحياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r15.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r15.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports an interpretation that God gives life through faith and death through unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r15.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي قولا إنه أحيا بالإيمان وأمات بالكفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r2.claim: God alone gives death and life, as also stated in 67:2.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r6.claim: One reading is that God ordains the causes of death and life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r7.claim: Ibn Bahr reads the phrase as creating death and life, as in 67:2.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r7.anchor: خلق الموت والحياة كما قال تعالى : { هو الذي خلق الموت والحياة } قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r8.claim: Life may mean fertility and death barrenness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r8.anchor: أن يريد بالحياة الخصب وبالموت الجدب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r9.claim: Another gloss is that God brings death through disobedience and life through obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r10.claim: The wording may refer to fathers dying and sons being born.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r11.claim: A further possible gloss is that God causes sleep and waking.

MUQATIL:53:43-50/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r2.claim: God causes the living to die and brings the dead to life.
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r2.anchor: { وأنه هو أمات } الأحياء { وأحيا } [آية: 44] الموتى
